questions.stem: In Year 4, an individual taxpayer purchased qualifying depreciable property for $2,800,000 and is making an election under Section 179. Assume the statutory maximum Section 179 expense is $1,020,000 with a $2,550,000 phase-out threshold. What amount, if any, is the taxpayer's Section 179 expense for Year 4?
questions.explanation:
The Section 179 election allows taxpayers to immediately expense certain property, rather than capitalize and depreciate it over multiple years. Qualifying property must be purchased from an unrelated party and used within the U.S. in an active trade or business, and be:

Tangible personal property (Section 1245 property),

Off-the-shelf computer software, or

Any of the following improvements to nonresidential real property after the building was placed in service:

Interior portion of a building (remodel)

Roof

Heating, ventilation, and air-conditioning property

Fire protection/alarm systems

Security systems

The maximum Section 179 expense for Year 4 is $1,020,000 (for 2020). This amount is reduced dollar-for-dollar when total purchases of qualifying property exceeds a $2,550,000 threshold. However, the allowable expense is ultimately limited to the taxpayer's business income.

Because the taxpayer's purchases exceed this threshold by $250,000 ($2,800,000 purchases − $2,550,000 threshold), the maximum Section 179 expense is reduced to $770,000 ($1,020,000 maximum expense − $250,000 excess purchases).

Note: Because the maximum deduction and threshold are adjusted annually, the exam will most likely provide the amounts to use.
questions.explanationJa: Section 179は、適格資産を資本化して減価償却する代わりに取得年度に即時費用化できる制度である。上限額$1,020,000は、適格資産の購入総額が閾値$2,550,000を超えた分だけ1ドル対1ドルで減額される。購入額は閾値を$250,000（$2,800,000 − $2,550,000）超えているため、Section 179費用は$770,000（$1,020,000 − $250,000）となる。なお、最終的な控除額は事業所得の範囲に制限される。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Property Tax Transactions Q.1

questions.stem:
A moving company purchased a truck in Year 1. The following information is available:

Sale price | $80,000
Title and license | 8,000
Vehicle insurance | 2,000
Salvage value | 15,000

What amount represents the truck's depreciable basis for federal tax purposes?
questions.explanationJa: 減価償却の基礎価額には、資産を取得し事業の用に供するまでに要した支出のみを含める。本問で取得に直接関係するのは購入価格と登録・ライセンス費用だけであり、保険料は期間費用である。また税務上（MACRS）は残存価額を考慮しない。したがって基礎価額は$80,000 + $8,000 = $88,000である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Property Tax Transactions Q.2

questions.stem: A taxpayer purchased and placed into service a $1,690,000 piece of equipment. The equipment is 7-year property having a 14.29% applicable depreciation rate for the first year. The taxpayer is making a Section 179 election but is elected out of any bonus depreciation. Assume that the maximum Section 179 limit is $1,020,000 and the threshold is $2,550,000. Before considering any depreciation deduction, the taxpayer had $2,700,000 of taxable business income. What is the maximum amount of cost recovery deduction this year?
questions.explanation:
Because the taxpayer elected out of bonus depreciation, the maximum cost recovery deduction consists of the allowable Section 179 expense and any regular depreciation. Purchased property ($1,690,000) did not exceed the $2,550,000 threshold, so the Section 179 expense is capped at the unreduced limit ($1,020,000).

The depreciable basis after the election affects the current depreciation as follows:

Depreciable basis (after election): = / $1,690,000 Total purchase − $1,020,000 Section 179 expense
=: $670,000
Current depreciation: = / $670,000 Depreciable basis × 14.29% Depreciation rate
=: $95,743
Maximum cost recovery deduction: = / $1,020,000 Section 179 expense + $95,743 Depreciation expense
=: $1,115,743
questions.explanationJa: ボーナス償却を選択しないため、最大の費用回収額はSection 179費用と通常の減価償却費の合計となる。購入額$1,690,000は閾値$2,550,000を超えず、事業所得$2,700,000も十分あるため、Section 179費用は上限の$1,020,000をそのまま使える。残りの基礎価額$670,000（$1,690,000 − $1,020,000）に初年度償却率14.29%を掛けた$95,743が通常の減価償却費である。合計は$1,020,000 + $95,743 = $1,115,743となる。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Property Tax Transactions Q.3

questions.stem: Xylo, a calendar-year C corporation, acquired the assets of Yerkes, also a calendar-year C corporation, on March 1 of the current year. One of the assets acquired was a trademark to which Xylo properly allocated $1,200,000 of the purchase price. What is Xylo's amortization deduction for the current year?
questions.explanation:
Using the straight-line method, the basis is amortized over 180 months (15 years) regardless of the intangible asset's useful life.

Xylo's amortization deduction is $6,666.70 per month ($1.2 million / 180 months) ("$30,000" / "$120,000"). Starting in March, Xylo may deduct 10 months of amortization totaling $66,667 ($6,666.70 × 10).
questions.explanationJa: 資産買収で取得した商標などのSection 197無形資産は、実際の耐用年数にかかわらず180か月（15年）で定額償却する。月額は$1,200,000 ÷ 180か月 = $6,666.70である。3月1日取得のため当年度は3月から12月までの10か月分を償却でき、$6,666.70 × 10 = $66,667となる。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Property Tax Transactions Q.4

questions.stem: On January 1, Fast, Inc. entered into a covenant not to compete with Swift, Inc. for a period of five years, with an option by Swift to extend it to seven years. What is the amortization period of the covenant for tax purposes?
questions.explanation:
Noncompete covenants often arise when one company acquires a division, product line, or technology from another company. These covenants protect the acquirer's investment by requiring that the seller agree not to compete with the acquirer in a specified market for a specified period. Because the covenant lacks physical substance and but provides an economic benefit, it is capitalized.

Using the straight-line method, the cost basis is amortized over 180 months (15 years) regardless of the intangible asset's useful life.

As an intangible asset, the noncompete covenant in this scenario must be amortized over 15 years even though it covers only a five-year period ("5 years."). In addition, the optional seven-year extension does not affect the amortization period ("7 years.").

("17 years.") Intangibles are amortized over 15 years, not 17 years.
questions.explanationJa: 競業避止契約は物理的実体はないが経済的便益をもたらすため資本化され、事業取得に伴う無形資産として180か月（15年）で定額償却する。契約期間が5年であっても、7年への延長オプションがあっても償却期間は変わらない。17年という期間も無形資産の償却期間ではない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Property Tax Transactions Q.5

questions.stem:
On May 1 of the prior year, Baker Co. purchased equipment with a five-year useful life for a cost of $10,000. Baker adopted the MACRS deprecation system and did not utilize any special depreciation deductions. On March 1 of the current year, Baker sold the equipment. The MACRS deprecation schedule for five-year property is listed below:

First year | 20.00%
Second year | 32.00%
Third year | 19.20%

What amount of depreciation can Baker deduct in the current year?
questions.explanation:
For most personal property, the half-year convention applies; this treats the asset as if it had been purchased and placed into service in the middle of the year. This results in allowing only 6 months (half,50%) of depreciation in the year of acquisition and year of disposal.

In this scenario, Baker Co. purchased five-year personal property. Using the MACRS schedule provided, the second-year deprecation rate is 32%. Because Baker disposed of the equipment in Year 2, only a half year (50%) of the depreciation is allowed. Accordingly, Baker may deduct $1,600 ($10,000 × 32% × 50%) in Year 2
questions.explanationJa: 大半の動産には期中半年規約（ハーフイヤー・コンベンション）が適用され、取得年度と処分年度はそれぞれ半年分のみ償却する。Baker Co.は5年資産を2年目に売却しているため、2年目の償却率32%の半分しか控除できない。したがって当年度の減価償却費は$10,000 × 32% × 50% = $1,600である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Property Tax Transactions Q.6

questions.stem: A taxpayer wants to deduct the cost of a seven-year asset placed in service this year. The cost qualifies for the Section 179 election to expense assets. Which of the following statements is most accurate regarding the immediate expensing of this asset versus the depreciation of this asset over seven years?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Depreciation provides a greater deduction over the life of the asset.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Section 179 provides a greater deduction over the life of the asset because, subject to limitations, the cost of the asset is deductible in full.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The cost of the asset may be deducted under both Section 179 and as depreciation.

choices.label: D
choices.text: There is no difference in the total amount that is deductible over the life of the asset.

questions.explanation: The Section 179 election allows taxpayers to immediately expense certain property rather than capitalize and depreciate it over multiple years. This incentivizes investment and simplifies tax compliance and recordkeeping related to depreciation. Although the timing of the deduction differs, the same total deduction for such property is taken under both methods. Note that salvage (residual) values are not used for tax purposes.
questions.explanationJa: Section 179は資産を複数年で減価償却する代わりに即時費用化できる制度であり、変わるのは控除のタイミングだけである。いずれの方法でも資産の耐用期間を通じた控除総額は同じになる。なお税務上は残存価額を考慮しない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Property Tax Transactions Q.7

questions.stem: In Year 1, a taxpayer had business income before depreciation of $3,000,000. In addition, the taxpayer purchased and placed in service $2,000,000 of depreciable property for business use. The taxpayer is electing to expense the property under Section 179 but is electing out of bonus depreciation. Assuming the Section 179 limit is $1,020,000 and the threshold is $2,550,000 in Year 1, what is the property's depreciable basis?
questions.explanation: Section 179 expense is limited to $1,020,000 but is reduced one dollar for every dollar spent on Section 179 property that exceeds a $2,550,000 threshold. Because the purchased property did not exceed this threshold, the taxpayer may expense $1,020,000 under Section 179. Therefore, the adjusted basis after the Section 179 expense is $980,000 ($2,000,000 purchased property − $1,020,000 limit)
questions.explanationJa: Section 179費用の上限$1,020,000は、適格資産の購入額が閾値$2,550,000を超えた分だけ減額される。購入額$2,000,000は閾値を超えておらず、事業所得$3,000,000も十分あるため、$1,020,000を全額費用化できる。したがってSection 179適用後の償却基礎価額は$2,000,000 − $1,020,000 = $980,000である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Property Tax Transactions Q.8

questions.stem:
On August 1, Year 1, Sound Co. purchased and placed into service an office building costing $264,000, which includes $30,000 for the land. The MACRS depreciation schedule for 27.5-year property and 39-year property placed in service in the 8th month is listed below.

27.5-year property | 1.364%
39-year property | 0.963%

What was Sound's MACRS deduction for the office building in that year?
questions.explanation: In this scenario, Sound Co. purchased an office building and land for $264,000. Land is not depreciable. Therefore, the depreciable basis is $234,000 ($264,000 cost − $30,000 land). Depreciation is $2,253 ($234,000 depreciable basis × 0.00963).
questions.explanationJa: 土地は減価償却できないため、購入額$264,000から土地分$30,000を除いた$234,000が建物の償却基礎価額となる。事務所ビルは非居住用不動産として39年資産であり、8月に供用した場合の償却率0.963%を用いる。減価償却費は$234,000 × 0.963% = $2,253である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Property Tax Transactions Q.9

questions.stem:
Lobster, Inc. purchased the following assets during Year 1:

Computers | $35,000
Computer desks | 22,000
Office furniture | 4,000
Delivery trucks | 25,000
Building | 425,000

What should be reported as the cost basis for MACRS seven-year property?
questions.explanation:
MACRS requires taxpayers to use established:

Depreciable life (5-year, 7-year)

Depreciation method (200% declining balance, straight-line)

Depreciation convention (mid-year convention, mid-quarter convention)

MACRS 7-year property is personal property that includes furniture (computer desks), fixtures, and equipment. Five-year property includes automobiles and transportation equipment (delivery trucks), and information system hardware (computers). Nonresidential real estate (office building) is classified as 39-year property.

In this scenario, Lobster, Inc. purchased 5 depreciable assets. Only the furniture (computer desks, office furniture) is reported as 7-year property under MACRS.

7-year property: = $22,000 computer desks + $4,000 office furniture
= $26,000 cost basis:
questions.explanationJa: MACRSでは、家具・什器・備品などが7年資産に分類される。コンピュータと配送トラックは5年資産、建物（非居住用不動産）は39年資産である。したがって7年資産はコンピュータデスク$22,000と事務用家具$4,000のみで、取得原価は$26,000となる。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Property Tax Transactions Q.10

questions.stem: A taxpayer placed in service a $3,100,000 piece of equipment during the year. The equipment is 7-year property. The first-year depreciation for 7-year property is 14.29%. Assume there is a Section 179 limit in the current year of $1,020,000 with a $2,550,000 threshold. What amount is the maximum allowable deduction related to property for the year if the taxpayer elects out of bonus depreciation?
questions.explanation:
Because the taxpayer elected out of bonus depreciation, the maximum allowable property related deduction consists of the allowable Section 179 expense and regular depreciation. Property purchased exceeded the threshold by $550,000 ($3,100,000 Purchases − $2,550,000 Threshold); therefore, the $3,100,000 purchase amount is capped at the reduced limit of $470,000 ($1,020,000 Statutory limit − $550,000 Excess purchase) ("$1,020,000").

Depreciable basis: = / $3,100,000 Property purchased − $470,000 Section 179 expense
=: $2,630,000
Current depreciation: = / $2,630,000 Depreciable basis × 14.29% Depreciation rate
=: $375,827
Property-related deduction: = / $470,000 Section 179 expense + $375,827 Current depreciation
=: $845,827
questions.explanationJa: ボーナス償却を選択しないため、最大控除額はSection 179費用と通常の減価償却費の合計となる。購入額$3,100,000は閾値$2,550,000を$550,000超えるため、Section 179の上限は$1,020,000 − $550,000 = $470,000に減額される。残りの基礎価額$2,630,000（$3,100,000 − $470,000）に14.29%を掛けた$375,827が通常の減価償却費である。合計は$470,000 + $375,827 = $845,827となる。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Property Tax Transactions Q.11

questions.stem:
Aircrew, Inc. purchased a van at a cost of $30,000 on February 1, Year 4. The van has an estimated useful life of 10 years and a salvage value of $2,000. Neither Section 179 expensing nor bonus depreciation were taken. No other assets were put into service in Year 4. The MACRS depreciation schedule is listed below:

Year | 3-year | 5-year | 7-year | 10-year
1 | 33.33% | 20.00% | 14.29% | 10.00%

What is Aircrew's MACRS depreciation for the van in Year 4?
questions.explanation: In this case, Aircrew, Inc. placed a $30,000 van in service in Year 4. Salvage value is ignored for MACRS, so the depreciable basis is $30,000. The van is five-year property under MACRS. From the MACRS table, the depreciation percentage is 20%, which includes the half-year convention. Aircrew s depreciation for the van is $6,000 ($30,000 depreciable basis × 20%).
questions.explanationJa: MACRSでは残存価額を考慮しないため、償却基礎価額は取得原価の$30,000である。耐用年数の見積り（10年）に関係なく、バンは5年資産に分類され、初年度の償却率20%（ハーフイヤー・コンベンション込み）を適用する。減価償却費は$30,000 × 20% = $6,000である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Property Tax Transactions Q.12

questions.stem:
Which of the following conditions must be satisfied for a taxpayer to expense, in the year of purchase, under Internal Revenue Code Section 179, the cost of new or used tangible depreciable personal property?
I. The property must be purchased for use in the taxpayer's active trade or business
II. The property must be purchased from an unrelated party
I | II
questions.explanation:
To qualify, the property must be purchased from an unrelated party and used primarily within the U.S. in an active trade or business, and it must be Section 179 property.

Section 179 property

Tangible personal property (Section 1245 property),

Off-the-shelf computer software, or

Certain improvements to a nonresidential building after the building's in-service date.
questions.explanationJa: Section 179の適用を受けるには、資産を関連当事者以外から購入し、主として米国内の能動的な事業の用に供する必要がある。さらに対象は有形動産（Section 1245資産）、市販のソフトウェア、一定の非居住用建物の改良などのSection 179資産に限られる。したがって、能動的な事業で使用することと、非関連者から購入することは、いずれも必要な条件である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Property Tax Transactions Q.13

questions.stem: A taxpayer owned land with a basis of $120,000, subject to a mortgage of $75,000. The taxpayer exchanged the land held for another parcel of land with a fair market value of $200,000 plus cash of $35,000, and the taxpayer was relieved of the mortgage on the relinquished land. The transaction qualified for like-kind exchange treatment. What amount of taxable gain will be recognized on the taxpayer's tax return for this exchange?
questions.explanation:
Like-kind exchange (LKE) is a nontaxable trade of investment/business real property (ie, qualified property) for similar qualified property. Although a gain is not recognized, the realized gain is deferred until the received property is disposed (eg, sold). The realized gain is the difference between the FMV of property (including boot) received and the adjusted basis of property (including boot) given.

To determine if the excess boot triggered a recognizable gain, the taxpayer must figure the realized gain or loss.

If a loss is realized, then the loss is not recognized.

If a gain is realized, the taxpayer must recognize the lesser of the net amount of boot received or the realized gain.

Because the taxpayer received more boot than given and realized a gain, a $110,000 gain (lesser of $110,000 net boot received or $190,000 realized gain) must be recognized.

Lesser of:
Net boot received: = / Boot received − Boot given
=: ($35,000 cash + $75,000 mortgage relief) − ($0 boot given)
=: $110,000 net amount of boot given
or:
Realized gain: = / Total FMV received − (Adjusted basis + Boot given)
=: ($200,000 land + $35,000 cash + $75,000 mortgage relief) − ($120,000 basis)
=: $310,000 received − $120,000 given
=: $190,000 realized gain
questions.explanationJa: 同種資産交換では実現利益は原則として繰り延べられるが、受け取ったボートがあれば、純受取ボートと実現利益のいずれか少ない額を認識する。受取ボートは現金$35,000と債務免除$75,000の合計$110,000で、支払ったボートはない。実現利益は受取総額$310,000（土地$200,000 + 現金$35,000 + 債務免除$75,000）から簿価$120,000を引いた$190,000である。両者のうち少ない$110,000が認識利益となる。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Property Tax Transactions Q.14

questions.stem: On January 15 of the current year, a taxpayer inherited stock worth $25,000. The decedent had purchased the stock in June of the previous year for $20,000, and the shares were worth $23,000 at date of death. The executor of the estate did not elect to use the alternate valuation date. In March of the current year, the taxpayer sold the stock for $27,000. What amount and type of gain should be reported by the taxpayer in the year of the sale?
questions.explanation:
The receipt of an inheritance by a beneficiary is nontaxable. Generally, FMV on the date of death, not the FMV when the inheritance was received or the decedent's adjusted basis of the property. The executor of the estate can elect to use the alternate valuation date instead.

The beneficiary's gain or loss is always reported as long term regardless of the actual holding period.

In this scenario, the beneficiary's basis was $23,000, the FMV of the property at date of death. When the stock (capital asset) was sold, a $4,000 ($27,000 − $23,000) long-term capital gain resulted, which should be reported in the year of the sale.
questions.explanationJa: 相続による財産の取得自体は非課税であり、受益者の基礎価額は原則として死亡日時点の公正価値となる（代替評価日は選択されていない）。受け取った日の価値$25,000や被相続人の取得原価$20,000は用いない。相続財産の売却は実際の保有期間にかかわらず常に長期として扱う。したがって$27,000 − $23,000 = $4,000の長期キャピタルゲインとなる。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Property Tax Transactions Q.15

questions.stem: A single individual had a net operating loss of $20,000 three years ago. A Code Sec. 1244 stock loss made up three-fourths of that loss. The taxpayer had no taxable income from that year until the current year. In the current year, the taxpayer has gross income of $80,000 and sustains another loss of $50,000 on Code Sec. 1244 stock. Assuming the entire $20,000 net operating loss is carried over to the current year, what are the amount and character of the Code Sec. 1244 loss that the taxpayer can deduct for the current year?
questions.explanation:
Disposition of a capital asset (stock) generally results in a capital gain or loss. Individual taxpayers may deduct up to $3,000 of a net capital loss each year. Any unused loss is carried forward indefinitely. However, to incentivize investment in small business, the IRS allows individuals who have sustained a loss on Section 1244 stock to reclassify part of a capital loss to an ordinary loss (No $3,000 limit).

The statutory amount that can be reclassified as an ordinary loss is $50,000 ($100,000 if married filing jointly). Any excess remains a capital loss. Because a Section 1244 loss is an ordinary loss, it may be treated as a trade or business loss when calculating an individual's NOL.

In this scenario, the individual has a current $50,000 Section 1244 loss. Because the total loss does not exceed the statutory limit, the entire $50,000 is reclassified as an ordinary loss and is fully deductible.
questions.explanationJa: 個人のキャピタルロスは通常年$3,000までしか控除できないが、Section 1244株式の損失は一定額まで通常損失（ordinary loss）として扱える。単身者の場合、その上限は年$50,000（夫婦合算申告なら$100,000）であり、超過分はキャピタルロスのままとなる。当年度のSection 1244損失は$50,000で上限を超えないため、全額$50,000が通常損失として控除できる。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Property Tax Transactions Q.16

questions.stem:
In Year 1, a taxpayer had the following transactions in Jacky, Inc. common stock:

Shares | Price
Jan. 1 -- Purchase | 500 | $25
May 12 -- Sale | 500 | $23
May 28 -- Purchase | 250 | $22
Oct. 15 -- Sale | 100 | $18

What is the taxpayer's deductible capital loss?
questions.explanation:
To prevent taxpayers from recognizing losses if they sell securities and buy them back shortly before or after the sale date, the wash sale rule was enacted. A wash sale occurs when securities are sold at a loss and the taxpayer acquires the same or substantially identical securities within 30 days before or after the sale.

Losses from wash sales are not deductible because the taxpayer's economic position does not change. The nondeductible loss is added to the basis of the acquired

If the number of shares acquired is less than the number originally purchased, the disallowed loss must be prorated (based on the shares acquired).

Because wash sales apply only to losses, gains are taxable.

In this scenario, on May 28, the taxpayer purchased back 250 (half) of the 500 shares sold on May 12. Because the purchase took place within 30 days of the May 12 sale, half of the loss incurred from the sale is disallowed and added to the basis of the stock acquired. In October (after more than 30 days), 100 shares were sold; the loss incurred from this sale is based on the new basis of the stock and is recognized. Therefore, the taxpayer recognizes $1,100 loss, as shown below.

Loss from May 12 sale: ($23 sales price − $25 cost) × 500 shares / = / $1,000 loss
Disallowed loss: $1,000 disallowed loss × 250/500 shares / = / $500 loss
Basis of 250 shares purchased on May 28: ($22 price × 250 shares) + $500 disallowed loss / = / $6,000 ($24 per share [$6,000/250])
Sold 100 shares on Oct. 15: ($18 sales price − $24 basis) × 100 shares / = / $600 recognized loss
Recognized loss: $1,000 − $500 + $600 = $1,100
questions.explanationJa: ウォッシュセール規定により、損失を出して売却した日の前後30日以内に同一銘柄を買い戻すと、その損失は否認され、買い戻した株式の基礎価額に加算される。5月12日の売却損$1,000（($23 − $25) × 500株）のうち、28日に500株中250株を買い戻したため半分の$500が否認され、損失は$500となる。買い戻した250株の基礎価額は$22 × 250株 + $500 = $6,000（1株$24）となる。10月15日の100株売却は30日超後なので損失($18 − $24) × 100株 = $600が認められ、控除できる損失は合計$500 + $600 = $1,100である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Property Tax Transactions Q.17

questions.stem: A taxpayer purchased 100 shares of Eastern Corp. stock for $18,000 on April 1 of the prior year. On February 1 of the current year, 50 shares of Eastern were sold for $7,000. Fifteen days later, the taxpayer purchased 25 shares of Eastern for $3,750. What is the amount of the taxpayer's recognized gain or loss?
questions.explanation:
In this scenario, 50 (half) of the original 100 shares purchased were sold by the taxpayer at a $2,000 loss on February 1. Because the taxpayer reacquired 25 (half) of the 50 shares 15 days later, a wash sale occurred. Half of the $2,000 loss is disallowed and added to the basis of the 25 shares reacquired. Therefore, the taxpayer's recognized loss is $1,000, as shown below.

Loss from Feb. 1 sale of 50 shares: [$7,000 sales price − ($18,000 cost × 50 sold / 100 shares acquired)] / = / $2,000
Less disallowed loss: $2,000 × (25 shares reacquired / 50 sold) / = / (1,000)
Recognized loss: = / $1,000

Note: The basis of the 25 reacquired shares is $4,750 ($3,750 + $1,000 disallowed loss).
questions.explanationJa: 2月1日に保有100株のうち50株を売却し、損失は$7,000 − $18,000 × 50/100 = $2,000である。15日後に売却株数50株の半分にあたる25株を買い戻したため、ウォッシュセールとなり損失の半分$1,000が否認される。したがって認識される損失は$2,000 − $1,000 = $1,000である。否認された$1,000は買い戻した25株の基礎価額に加算され、$3,750 + $1,000 = $4,750となる。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Property Tax Transactions Q.18

questions.stem:
In Year 4, a taxpayer had the following transactions:

Sold business equipment owned for 3 years for $10,000. The carrying value at the time of sale was $15,000.
Was informed that a friend declared bankruptcy who still owed the taxpayer $4,000 on a $12,000 nonbusiness loan made two years ago.
Sold stock for $3,000 gain that was inherited during the year.

What is the amount and character of the taxpayer's net capital gain or loss for Year 4 before any limitations?

choices.label: D
choices.text: $1,000 short-term capital loss and a $5,000 long-term capital loss.

questions.explanation:
The disposal of a capital asset results in a gain or loss being classified as long term (LT) or short term (ST), depending on the holding period. These gains and losses are netted to produce an overall net capital gain or loss. For simplicity, some capital assets have statutory holding periods (nonbusiness bad debts are ST, inherited property is LT).

Section 1231 assets (equipment) are assets used in a trade or business that are held longer than 1 year. The sale of such property results in a Section 1231 gain or losses. The net Section 1231 loss is treated as an ordinary loss, which offsets ordinary income.

In this scenario, the $5,000 equipment loss (Section 1231 asset) is treated as an ordinary loss. The $4,000 nonbusiness bad debt is a ST capital loss while the $3,000 gain from the sale of the inherited stock is a LT capital gain. This results in a net $1,000 ST capital loss, not LT
questions.explanationJa: 事業用設備（1年超保有）はSection 1231資産であり、純Section 1231損失は通常損失として扱われるため、設備の売却損$5,000はキャピタルロスに含めない。非事業用貸倒れ$4,000は保有期間にかかわらず短期キャピタルロス、相続株式の売却益$3,000は常に長期キャピタルゲインとなる。これらを相殺すると純額$1,000の短期キャピタルロスとなる。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Property Tax Transactions Q.19

questions.stem: In Year 1, Cowabunga Corp. purchased machinery for $1,000,000 and elected to expense $600,000 under Section 179. In Year 3, Cowabunga sold the machinery for $930,000, with an adjusted basis of $200,000. What amount of gain must be reported as ordinary gain for tax purposes?
questions.explanation:
In this scenario, Cowabunga Corp. recognized a total gain of $730,000. The recapture under Section 1245 as ordinary income is limited to $730,000. The $600,000 Section 179 expense is included in the $800,000(accumulated depreciation), subject to recapture as annual depreciation.

Sales price |  | $930,000
Cost | $1,000,000
Accumulated depreciation | $800,000
Adjusted basis |  | (200,000)
Gain on sale |  | $730,000
Section 1245 recapture |  | (730,000)
Long-term capital gain |  | $0
questions.explanationJa: 売却価額$930,000から調整後基礎価額$200,000を引いた売却益は$730,000である。Section 179の即時費用化額$600,000も含め、減価償却累計額は$800,000（$1,000,000 − $200,000）となる。Section 1245資産では、減価償却累計額と売却益のいずれか少ない額が通常所得としてリキャプチャーされるため、$730,000全額が通常所得となり、長期キャピタルゲインは残らない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Property Tax Transactions Q.20

questions.stem: When a corporation has an unused net capital loss that is carried back or carried forward to another tax year

choices.label: A
choices.text: It retains its original identity as short-term or long-term.

choices.label: B
choices.text: It is treated as a short-term capital loss whether or not it was short-term when sustained.

choices.label: C
choices.text: It is treated as a long-term capital loss whether or not it was long-term when sustained.

choices.label: D
choices.text: It can be used to offset ordinary income up to the amount of the carryback or carryover.

questions.explanation:
When C corporations net their capital gains and losses, the result is either an overall net capital gain or net capital loss. An overall net capital gain is included as ordinary income. However, if a net capital loss results, no deduction is allowed against ordinary income. A net capital loss may offset only capital gains.

The use of capital losses is restricted to offsetting capital gains to prevent corporations from significantly reducing their taxable income in any single tax year (by selling off capital assets) to substantially lower their taxes. Corporations must carry back any unused net capital losses 3 years to offset (reduce) any prior capital gains, as follows:

Any remaining loss is then carried forward to offset future capital gains for up to 5 years.

To simplify recordkeeping and because corporations do not receive a preferential tax rate for capital gains, all corporate net capital losses that are carried back or forward are considered short-term capital losses regardless of their actual nature
questions.explanationJa: C法人の純キャピタルロスは通常所得と相殺できず、キャピタルゲインとのみ相殺できる。未使用分は3年繰り戻し、残りは5年繰り越す。記録を簡素化するため、また法人にはキャピタルゲインの優遇税率がないため、繰り戻し・繰り越されたキャピタルロスは本来の性質にかかわらずすべて短期キャピタルロスとして扱う。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Property Tax Transactions Q.21

questions.stem:
An individual reports the following capital transactions in the current year:

Short-term capital gain | $ 1,000
Short-term capital loss | 11,000
Long-term capital gain | 10,000
Long-term capital loss | 6,000

What amount is deducted in arriving at adjusted gross income?
questions.explanation:
In this scenario, the individual starts the netting by holding period that produces a $4,000 net LT capital gain and a $10,000 net ST loss. These amounts are netted one more time, resulting in an overall net $6,000 ST capital loss. However, the deduction is limited to $3,000. The unused loss ($6,000 − $3,000 = $3,000) is carried forward.

LT capital gain | $10,000
LT capital loss | (6,000)
Net LT capital gain |  | $ 4,000
ST capital gain | 1,000
ST capital loss | (11,000)
Net ST capital gain |  | (10,000)
Net capital loss |  | $ (6,000)
Deductible capital loss (limited) $3,000:
questions.explanationJa: まず保有期間ごとに損益を相殺する。長期は$10,000 − $6,000 = $4,000の純利益、短期は$1,000 − $11,000 = $10,000の純損失となる。両者を相殺すると$6,000の純短期キャピタルロスとなるが、個人が通常所得から控除できるのは年$3,000までである。したがってAGI算定上の控除額は$3,000で、残り$3,000は翌年以降に繰り越す。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Property Tax Transactions Q.22

questions.stem: Bluff purchased equipment for business use for $35,000 and made $1,000 of improvements to the equipment. After deducting depreciation of $5,000, Bluff gave the equipment to Russett for business use. At the time the gift was made, the equipment had a fair market value of $32,000. Ignoring gift tax consequences, what is Russett's basis in the equipment?
questions.explanation: In this scenario, the FMV of the equipment on the date of the gift to Russett was $32,000. Bluff's adjusted basis was $31,000 ($35,000 cost + $1,000 improvements − $5,000 depreciation). Because the FMV was greater than the adjusted basis, Russett's basis in the equipment is the carryover basis of $31,000.
questions.explanationJa: 贈与時点の公正価値$32,000は、贈与者の調整後基礎価額$31,000（取得原価$35,000 + 改良費$1,000 − 減価償却$5,000）を上回っている。公正価値が贈与者の基礎価額以上の場合、受贈者は贈与者の基礎価額を引き継ぐ。したがってRussettの基礎価額は$31,000である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Property Tax Transactions Q.23

questions.stem:
In Year 1, an individual taxpayer purchased a condominium used as rental property at a cost of $180,000. The taxpayer sold the condominium for $200,000 in Year 3. The condominium had an adjusted basis of $161,000 and accumulated depreciation of $19,000 using straight-line depreciation under the MACRS. How should the taxpayer report the gain in Year 3?
Ordinary gain | Unrecaptured Sec. 1250 gain | Long-term capital gain
questions.explanation:
In general, Section 1231 property comprises any depreciable assets or land used in a trade or business and held for more than one year. Section 1231 assets include Section 1245 assets (personal property) and Section 1250 assets (real property, including land). Over the life of the assets, depreciation (or amortization) deductions are taken, reducing ordinary taxable income.

To encourage investment in business assets, net Section 1231 gains are treated as long-term capital gains while net section 1231 losses are treated as ordinary losses. This preferential treatment allows gains to offset any capital losses, which are fully deductible. However, a portion of the gain results from prior depreciation deductions and must be recaptured (reclassified).

For individuals selling Section 1250 property, the lesser of the accumulated depreciation or realized gain is reclassified as unrecaptured Section 1250 gain. This is taxed at a maximum rate of 25%. Any gain exceeding the recaptured amount is the result of the property's appreciation above the original cost and is generally treated as long-term capital gain.

In this scenario, the taxpayer recognized a $39,000 total gain. The lesser of the $39,000 gain or the $19,000 accumulated depreciation must be reclassified as unrecaptured Section 1250 gain. The remaining $20,000 is Section 1231 gain, taxed as a capital gain.

Sales price |  | $200,000
Cost | $180,000
Accumulated depreciation | (19,000)
Adjusted basis | $161,000 | (161,000)
Gain on sale |  | $39,000
Unrecaptured Section 1250 gain |  | (19,000)
Long-term capital gain |  | $20,000
questions.explanationJa: 賃貸用コンドミニアムはSection 1250資産（不動産）である。売却益は売却価額$200,000から調整後基礎価額$161,000を引いた$39,000となる。個人がSection 1250資産を売却した場合、減価償却累計額と売却益のいずれか少ない$19,000が「未回収Section 1250利得」となり、最高25%の税率で課税される。残りの$20,000はSection 1231利得として長期キャピタルゲインの扱いとなる。定額法で償却しているため、通常所得となる額は$0である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Property Tax Transactions Q.24

questions.stem: On July 1, Year 4, a donor gave a taxpayer a gift of stock worth $19,000. The donor purchased the stock for $20,000 in Year 1. On November 1, Year 4, the taxpayer sold the stock to an unrelated party for $18,500. What is the amount and character of the taxpayer's gain or loss upon the sale?
questions.explanation:
Generally, a taxpayer's basis for property received as a gift equals the donor's　adjusted basis (carried over). However, if the gift's FMV is less than the donor's adjusted basis when gifted (property has declined in value), the donee must keep track of dual basis (both donor's adjusted basis and FMV).

If the gift is later sold for:

More than the donor's adjusted basis, the donor's adjusted basis is used to calculate the gain and the donor's holding period carries over

Less than FMV when gifted, the FMV is used to calculate the loss and the donee's holding period begins on the date of the gift

An amount between FMV when gifted and the donor's adjusted basis, no gain/loss is recognized

These rules minimize the gain or loss realized by the donee and do not tax the donee on subsequent appreciation up to the donor's adjusted basis.

In this case, When gifted, the stock's FMV ($19,000) was less than the donor's adjusted basis ($20,000); therefore, the taxpayer's basis and holding period are determined by the sale. Since the stock sold ($18,500) for less than the FMV at the time of gift, the FMV at the time of gift is used as the basis to calculate the $500 loss ($18,500 sale − $19,000 basis).　The holding period begins on the date of gift which is July １, Year ４. Thus, it is short term.
questions.explanationJa: 贈与時の公正価値$19,000が贈与者の基礎価額$20,000を下回るため、受贈者は二重の基礎価額を管理する。売却額$18,500は贈与時の公正価値を下回るので、損失の計算には公正価値$19,000を用い、損失は$18,500 − $19,000 = $500となる。この場合、保有期間は贈与日（Year 4の7月1日）から始まり、11月1日の売却までは1年以内のため短期となる。したがって$500の短期キャピタルロスである。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Property Tax Transactions Q.25

questions.stem:
An individual taxpayer incurred the following transactions during Year 3:

April 2: Sold for a $6,000 gain, shares of stock purchased on May 1, Year 1.
May 15: Sold for a $2,000 gain, land used in the taxpayer's business which was purchased on July 1, Year 1.
June 3: Sold for a $3,000 loss, equipment used in the taxpayer's business which had been purchased on January 2, Year 2.
July 9: Sold for a $4,000 loss shares of stock inherited on February 22, Year 3.

What will the taxpayer report on the Year 3 tax return from these transactions?

choices.label: C
choices.text: $1,000 ordinary loss, $2,000 net long-term capital gain.

choices.label: D
choices.text: $3,000 ordinary loss, $4,000 net long-term capital gain.

questions.explanation:
Section 1231 assets (land, equipment) are assets used in a trade or business that are held longer than 1 year. The sale of such property results in Section 1231 gains and losses, which are netted. To allow the most favorable treatment of either a gain or loss:

A net Section 1231 gain is treated as a LT capital gain and included in the capital gain netting process, and

A net Section 1231 loss is treated as an ordinary loss, which may offset ordinary income.

In this scenario, the $2,000 gain from selling the land (Section 1231 asset) is netted against the $3,000 loss from selling the equipment (Section 1231 asset). The net $1,000 loss is treated as an ordinary loss. The taxpayer has a net $2,000 LT capital gain after netting the $4,000 LT capital loss from selling the inherited stock (always LT) against the $6,000 LT capital gain from the April 2 stock sale.
questions.explanationJa: 事業用の土地と設備は1年超保有しているためSection 1231資産であり、土地の利益$2,000と設備の損失$3,000を相殺すると純額$1,000の損失となり、これは通常損失として扱う。株式は資本資産であり、Year 1の5月1日に取得した株式の利益$6,000は長期となる。相続株式の損失$4,000も常に長期として扱う。両者を相殺すると$2,000の純長期キャピタルゲインとなる。したがって$1,000の通常損失と$2,000の純長期キャピタルゲインを報告する。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Property Tax Transactions Q.26

questions.stem:
A taxpayer sold land with an adjusted basis of $60,000 to a nephew for its fair market value of $50,000. The nephew later sold the land to an unrelated party for $55,000. What is the taxpayer's recognized loss upon the sale to the nephew? What is the nephew's recognized gain or loss upon the subsequent sale?
Taxpayer's Recognized Loss | Nephew's Recognized Gain or Loss
questions.explanation:
To prevent taxpayers from creating artificial tax losses by selling and exchanging property among family members, losses on the sale or exchange of property are not allowed for transactions between related parties.

For this purpose of disallowing losses on sales, family members include only the taxpayer's ancestors (parents, grandparents, great-grandparents), lineal descendants (children, grandchildren, great-grandchildren), spouse, and siblings; they do not include, for example, nieces, nephews, aunts, uncles, cousins, in-laws, stepparents, or stepsiblings. The definition of "related party" is different in some parts of the tax code, but this particular definition is used frequently in many parts of the tax code.

In a related transaction, the acquiring related party may later deduct the disallowed loss upon subsequently selling the property to an unrelated party. However, the deductible loss is limited to any gain on the subsequent sale.

Because the land in this scenario was sold to a nephew, the transaction is not with a related party. Therefore, the taxpayer may recognize (deduct) the $10,000 loss ($50,000 sale − $60,000 basis). In addition, the nephew cannot use the loss to reduce the $5,000 gain ($55,000 sale − $50,000 basis) recognized on the subsequent sale.
questions.explanationJa: 関連当事者間の売買損失は否認されるが、この規定上の家族は祖先・直系卑属・配偶者・兄弟姉妹に限られ、甥や姪は含まれない。したがって甥への売却は関連当事者取引に当たらず、納税者は$60,000 − $50,000 = $10,000の損失を認識できる。甥は取得価額$50,000を基礎価額とし、その後の売却で$55,000 − $50,000 = $5,000の利益を認識する。関連当事者取引ではないため、この利益を納税者の損失で減額することもできない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Property Tax Transactions Q.27

questions.stem: A taxpayer made a gift of property to a friend. The taxpayer's basis in the property was $1,200. The fair market value at the time of the gift was $1,400. The friend sold the property for $2,500. What was the amount of the friend's gain on the disposition?
questions.explanation:
If the gift is appreciated property (FMV when gifted > donor's adjusted basis), the donee's basis and holding period are the same as the donor's. Therefore, when the donee sells the property, any gain or loss is recognized based on the carryover adjusted basis.

In this scenario, because the gift was appreciated property ($1,400 FMV when gifted > $1,200 adjusted basis), the friend assumed the taxpayer's carryover basis ($1,200). Accordingly, the friend's gain on disposition of the property was $1,300 ($2,500 sales price − $1,200 basis).
questions.explanationJa: 贈与時の公正価値$1,400が贈与者の基礎価額$1,200を上回る値上がり資産の場合、受贈者は贈与者の基礎価額と保有期間を引き継ぐ。したがって友人の基礎価額は$1,200であり、売却益は$2,500 − $1,200 = $1,300となる。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Property Tax Transactions Q.28

questions.stem: In Year 4, a taxpayer purchased a house for $240,000 to use as their principal residence. Capital improvements costing $15,000 were made in Year 8. After living in the home for 5 years, the taxpayer sold it in Year 9 for $400,000. What is the tax treatment of the sale of the taxpayer's home in Year 9?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A $145,000 gain is realized and recognized.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A $145,000 gain is realized and $0 is recognized.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A $160,000 gain is realized and recognized.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A $160,000 gain is realized and $0 is recognized.

questions.explanation:
To encourage home ownership, the IRC allows taxpayers to take a statutory exclusion for all or part of the realized capital gain on the sale of their personal residence. Homeowners may exclude up to $250,000 ($500,000 if filing jointly) if the following ownership, use, and frequency requirements are met:

The taxpayer has owned and used the property as their principal residence for at least 2 years (not required to be continuous years) during the 5-year period ending on the sale date.

The taxpayer has not previously used the exclusion within 2 years of the sale date.

The realized gain (sales price − adjusted basis of house) less the exclusion is the recognized gain reported on the tax return. If no gain is recognized (the realized gain is offset by the exclusion), then none of the sale proceeds are taxable.

In this case, the taxpayer is eligible for the exclusion. The $250,000 exclusion eliminated the $145,000 realized gain. Therefore, no gain is recognized on the tax return.

Sales price: $400,000
Adjusted basis ($240,000 cost + $15,000 improvements): (255,000)
Realized gain: $145,000
Less exclusion (up to $250,000): (145,000)
Recognized gain: $0
questions.explanationJa: 主たる住居の売却では、売却日前5年間のうち2年以上所有かつ居住し、過去2年以内にこの除外を使っていなければ、利益のうち最大$250,000（夫婦合算申告は$500,000）を除外できる。調整後基礎価額は取得価額$240,000に改良費$15,000を加えた$255,000で、実現利益は$400,000 − $255,000 = $145,000となる。納税者は5年間居住しており除外の要件を満たすため、$145,000の実現利益は全額除外され、認識される利益は$0である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Property Tax Transactions Q.29

questions.stem:
A taxpayer exchanged investment real estate with a $375,000 fair market value (FMV), a $125,000 adjusted basis, and a $75,000 mortgage for similar investment property with a $260,000 FMV that was subject to a $40,000 mortgage, which the taxpayer assumed. In addition, the taxpayer received $50,000 cash and a vehicle with a $30,000 FMV, and the other party assumed the $75,000 mortgage. How much gain did the taxpayer recognize on the exchange, and what is the basis in the new real estate?
Gain recognized | Basis of new real estate
questions.explanationJa: 支払ったボートは引き受けた債務$40,000、受け取ったボートは現金$50,000・車両$30,000・債務免除$75,000の計$155,000であり、純受取ボートは$115,000となる。実現利益は$375,000 − $125,000 = $250,000である。認識利益は純受取ボートと実現利益のいずれか少ない$115,000となる。新不動産の基礎価額は、旧資産の基礎価額$125,000 + 支払ボート$40,000 − 受取ボート$155,000 + 認識利益$115,000 = $125,000である。繰延利益$135,000（$250,000 − $115,000）を公正価値$260,000から引いても同じ$125,000になる。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Property Tax Transactions Q.30

questions.stem: Sky Co., a C corporation, purchased a building for $500,000 in Year 1. In Year 11, Sky sold the building for $450,000. The building had accumulated depreciation of $128,000 using the straight-line depreciation method. What amount must Sky recapture as ordinary income in Year 11?
questions.explanation:
Section 1250 depreciable property is held by a C corporation and is sold at a gain, part of the gain is recaptured as ordinary income.

Specifically, Section 291 requires C corporations to recapture a statutory 20% of the lesser of the depreciation taken or the total gain as ordinary income( for Section 1250 assets only). Any remaining gain is Section 1231 gain, which is generally treated as a capital gain.

In this scenario, the $78,000 total gain is less than the $128,000 depreciation taken. Therefore, the total gain is used to calculate recapture. Accordingly, Sky Co. must recapture $15,600 as ordinary income.

Sales price |  | $450,000
Cost | $500,000
Accumulated depreciation | (128,000)
Adjusted basis |  | (372,000)
Gain on sale |  | $78,000
Section 291 recapture = $78,000 × 20% = $15,600:

("$25,600") A $25,600 ordinary gain would result if 20% of depreciation ($128,000) was used instead of gain. Section 291 recapture is based on the lesser of the depreciation or gain.

("$78,000") A $78,000 ordinary gain would treat the building as Section 1245 property, which requires the lesser of the gain or depreciation taken to be treated as ordinary income.
questions.explanationJa: C法人がSection 1250資産（建物）を売却益で処分すると、Section 291により、減価償却累計額と売却益のいずれか少ない額の20%を通常所得としてリキャプチャーする。調整後基礎価額は$500,000 − $128,000 = $372,000、売却益は$450,000 − $372,000 = $78,000で、減価償却累計額$128,000より少ない。したがってリキャプチャー額は$78,000 × 20% = $15,600である。減価償却額の20%（$25,600）や売却益全額（$78,000、Section 1245資産として扱った場合）ではない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Property Tax Transactions Q.31

questions.stem: On January 1, Smith sold land to Baker for $100,000 cash plus a note for $200,000 plus adequate interest with a $30,000 principal payment due in the second year. Smith's basis in the property was $100,000. What is the amount of the gain recognized in the second year under the installment method?
questions.explanation: Smith has a gross profit of $200,000 ($300,000 in net proceeds − $100,000 basis). Therefore, the gross profit percentage is 66.67% ($200,0000 gross profit ÷ $300,000 contract amount) of the payment received. Accordingly, $20,000 (66.67% × $30,000 down payment) of the payment received in the second year should be included in the gross income.
questions.explanationJa: 契約価額は現金$100,000と手形$200,000の合計$300,000で、基礎価額$100,000を引いた売上総利益は$200,000である。売上総利益率は$200,000 ÷ $300,000 = 66.67%となる。割賦販売法では受け取った元本にこの率を掛けた額を各年の利益として認識するため、2年目の元本受取額$30,000に対する認識利益は66.67% × $30,000 = $20,000である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Property Tax Transactions Q.32

questions.stem: Which of the following costs are subject to the Uniform Capitalization rules for manufactured tangible personal property?
questions.explanation:
Uniform Capitalization (UNICAP) rules (Section 263A) require taxpayers to capitalize all direct costs (materials, labor) and certain allocable indirect costs (overhead costs) to:

Real and personal tangible property produced by the taxpayer, and

Property acquired for resale by retailers, wholesalers, and distributors.

The UNICAP rules were created to provide consistency among taxpayers for determining inventory costs and to accelerate tax revenues by capitalizing certain inventory costs instead of expensing them as period costs. Because the rules were designed to affect larger resellers and manufacturers, taxpayers that have average annual gross receipts of $26 million (adjusted for inflation) or less for the three preceding tax years are exempt from UNICAP.

For property produced by manufacturers, capitalized costs include expenditures for purchasing, manufacturing (direct and indirect costs), and holding the property until sold. Accordingly, manufacturers must capitalize a portion of administrative, engineering, and overhead costs (associated with holding the inventory). Examples of such costs are taxes (other than income taxes) and warehouse storage.

However, nonmanufacturing costs such as selling, advertising, marketing, and research and development expenditures are expensed as incurred
questions.explanationJa: 統一資本化ルール（UNICAP、Section 263A）では、製造業者は直接費（材料・労務費）に加え、製造や在庫保有に配分される一定の間接費も資産の取得原価に算入しなければならない。資本化される間接費の例には、法人税等以外の租税や倉庫保管費がある。一方、販売費、広告費、マーケティング費、研究開発費は製造以外の費用として発生時に費用処理する。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Property Tax Transactions Q.33

questions.stem: An individual entered into several exchanges during the current tax year. Which of the following exchanges is classified as like-kind?
questions.explanation:
A like-kind exchange is a tax deferred (currently nontaxable) trade of qualified real property (land, buildings) held for productive use in a business or held for investment. The term "like-kind" refers to the property's character (use) and class (real estate), not the grade or quality.

For example, an exchange of personal residences (real property) would not qualify as a like-kind exchange since the use of the property is personal. However, land, whether unimproved or improved, is qualified property if it is held for investment or used in a trade or business.

In this scenario, unimproved land held for investment is exchanged for an apartment building that is used in a trade or business. If both properties are in the U.S., this qualifies for a like-kind exchange.

("Partnership interest for partnership interest." / "Common stock for common stock.") Partnership interests and common stock are not real property and therefore are not qualified property for a like-kind exchange.

("Manufacturing equipment for factory building.") Although an exchange of manufacturing equipment for factory building involves business-use assets, both must be real property. Equipment is depreciable personal property.
questions.explanationJa: 同種資産交換は、事業用または投資用に保有する不動産同士の交換に限られる。「同種」とは不動産という性質や用途を指し、品質や等級は問わない。そのため未改良の土地とアパートは、いずれも米国内の事業用・投資用不動産であれば同種資産交換に該当する。パートナーシップ持分や普通株式は不動産ではなく、製造設備は動産であるため対象外となる。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Property Tax Transactions Q.34

questions.stem:
Lobster, Inc. incurs the following losses on disposition of business assets during the year:

Loss on the sale of a building (straight-line depreciation taken in prior years: $200,000): $250,000
Loss on the abandonment of office equipment: 25,000
Loss on the sale of delivery trucks: 15,000

What is the amount and character of the losses to be reported on Lobster's tax return?
questions.explanation:
Section 1231 assets are assets used in a trade or business that are held longer than one year. These assets include depreciable personal property (equipment, vehicles) referred to as Section 1245 property and real property (land, buildings) known as Section 1250 property.

The disposal (sale, abandonment) of such assets results in Section 1231 gains and losses that are initially netted. To allow the most favorable treatment of either a gain or loss:

A net Section 1231 gain is added to other long-term capital gains and included in the capital gain/loss netting process, but

A net Section 1231 loss is treated as an ordinary loss, which offsets ordinary income and is never treated as a capital loss.

In addition, Sections 1245 and 1250 property is subject to deprecation recapture (reclassifying part of potential capital gain as ordinary gain). However, the recapture applies only if the property is sold at a gain (not a loss).

In this scenario, Lobster, Inc. had $40,000 of Section 1245 losses from the abandonment of the office equipment ($25,000) and the sale of delivery trucks ($15,000). There is a $250,000 Section 1250 loss from the sale of the building. After the Section 1231 netting process, Lobster reports an ordinary loss of $290,000 ($40,000 + $250,000).
questions.explanationJa: 事業で1年超保有した資産（動産であるSection 1245資産、不動産であるSection 1250資産）の売却や廃棄から生じた損益はSection 1231損益として相殺する。純損失は通常損失となり、キャピタルロスとして扱われることはない。減価償却のリキャプチャーは利益が出た場合のみ適用され、損失には関係しない。したがって建物の売却損$250,000、事務機器の廃棄損$25,000、トラックの売却損$15,000の合計$290,000がSection 1231損失（通常損失）となる。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Property Tax Transactions Q.35

questions.stem: A taxpayer inherited property from a parent. The property had an adjusted basis to the parent of $1,600,000. It was valued at $2,000,000 at the date of death and valued at $1,800,000 six months after the date of death. The executor elected the alternative valuation date. What is the taxpayer's basis in the property?
questions.explanation:
An heir's basis in inherited property is generally the FMV used for estate tax purposes. In general, this is the FMV on the date of death. However, the estate's executor may elect the alternative valuation date (AVD) (six months after the date of death). If elected, the heir's basis is the FMV on the earlier of:

The date the property was transferred to the heir or

Six months after the date of death.

In this scenario, the parent's estate valued the property on the AVD $1,800,000. Because nothing states that the property was transferred before the AVD, the taxpayer's basis in the property is the FMV on the AVD $1,800,000
questions.explanationJa: 相続財産の基礎価額は、原則として遺産税評価に用いた公正価値である。遺言執行者が代替評価日（死亡日から6か月後）を選択した場合、財産が相続人に移転された日と代替評価日のいずれか早い日の公正価値を用いる。本問では代替評価日前に移転されたという事実はないため、代替評価日の$1,800,000が基礎価額となる。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Property Tax Transactions Q.36

questions.stem: On June 1, Year 2, a taxpayer received a gift of stock worth $10,000. The donor had purchased the stock on March 1, Year 1, for $13,000. The taxpayer sold the stock to an unrelated party on August 1, Year 2, for $13,500. What is the amount and character of the taxpayer's gain or loss upon the sale?
questions.explanation:
Generally, a taxpayer's basis for property received as a gift equals the donor's　adjusted basis (carried over). However, if the gift's FMV is less than the donor's adjusted basis when gifted （property has declined in value), the donee must keep track of dual basis (both donor's adjusted basis and FMV).

If the gift is later sold for:

More than the donor's adjusted basis, the donor's adjusted basis is used to calculate the gain and the donor's holding period carries over

Less than FMV when gifted, the FMV is used to calculate the loss and the donee's holding period begins on the date of the gift

An amount between FMV when gifted and the donor's adjusted basis, no gain/loss is recognized

These rules minimize the gain or loss realized by the donee and do not tax the donee on subsequent appreciation up to the donor's adjusted basis ($13,000).

In this case, when the stock (capital asset) was gifted, the FMV was less than the donor's adjusted basis. Therefore, the taxpayer has dual basis for the property ($13,000 if sold for a gain and $10,000 if sold for a loss). Because the $13,500 sale price exceeds the $13,000 donor's basis, the gain is $500 and the holding period carried over begins on March 1, Year 1 (long-term). Accordingly, the taxpayer will report a $500 long-term capital gain.
questions.explanationJa: 贈与時の公正価値$10,000が贈与者の基礎価額$13,000を下回るため、受贈者は二重の基礎価額を持つ（利益の計算には$13,000、損失の計算には$10,000）。売却額$13,500は贈与者の基礎価額を上回るため、$13,000を用いて利益$500を計算する。この場合は贈与者の保有期間（Year 1の3月1日から）を引き継ぐため長期となる。したがって$500の長期キャピタルゲインである。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Property Tax Transactions Q.37

questions.stem:
In Year 9, MMI Corporation incurred net capital losses that amounted to $15,000. MMI's net capital gains/losses in prior years were as follows:

Year | Gain (loss)
3 | $3,000
4 | (1,000)
5 | 5,000
6 | 1,000
7 | 1,000
8 | 1,000

What amount of capital loss may MMI carry forward to Year 10?
questions.explanation:
In this scenario, MMI Corporation had a net capital loss of $15,000 in Year 9. MMI cannot deduct the capital loss in Year 9 but instead must carry it back three years, starting with Year 6. After offsetting capital gains in Years 6 through 8, the remaining $12,000 must then be carried forward to Year 10 and beyond (up to Year 14).

Year | Gain | Carryback used | Remaining carryback
6 | $1,000 | ($1,000) | $14,000
7 | 1,000 | (1,000) | 13,000
8 | 1,000 | (1,000) | 12,000
questions.explanationJa: C法人はYear 9の純キャピタルロス$15,000を当期に控除できず、3年前のYear 6から順に繰り戻して過去のキャピタルゲインと相殺する。Year 6・7・8の各$1,000と相殺すると$3,000が使われ、残りは$15,000 − $3,000 = $12,000となる。この$12,000をYear 10以降へ（5年間）繰り越す。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Property Tax Transactions Q.38

questions.stem: In a "like-kind" exchange of an investment asset for a similar asset that will also be held as an investment, no taxable gain or loss will be recognized on the transaction if both assets consist of

choices.label: D
choices.text: Rental real estate located in different states.

questions.explanation:
A like-kind exchange is a tax-deferred (nontaxable when exchanged) trade of qualified real property (land, buildings) held for productive use in a business or held for investment. The term "like-kind" refers to the property's character (use) and class (real estate), not the grade or quality.

For example, an exchange of depreciable personal property used in a business (equipment) would not qualify as a like-kind exchange. Securities (eg, convertible debentures, convertible preferred stock), although held for investment, do not qualify because they are not real property. The exchange of rental real estate qualifies regardless of what state the properties are located; however, the properties must be in the U.S.
questions.explanationJa: 同種資産交換は、事業用または投資用に保有する不動産同士の交換に限られる。転換社債や転換優先株式、パートナーシップ持分は投資目的で保有していても不動産ではないため対象外である。賃貸不動産同士の交換は、米国内であれば所在する州が異なっても同種資産交換として利益・損失を認識しない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Property Tax Transactions Q.39

questions.stem: On June 19, Year 1, an individual executed a short sale of 100 shares of stock at $10 per share. On June 19, Year 1, the individual covered and delivered the 100 shares at $8 per share. What is the character of gain or loss on the short sale?
questions.explanation:
Taxpayers who believe a stock price will decrease can use a short sale in the hope of realizing a gain by "selling high" and then "buying low." A short sale is executed by selling borrowed stock and involves four steps.

Borrow stock from a broker for a fee.

Sell the borrowed stock at market price (open the short sale) to obtain cash.

Purchase substantially identical property (cover the short sale) later at a lower price using cash from the sale.

Deliver substantially identical property back to the broker (close the short sale).

Gain or loss on a short sale is calculated in the usual manner for a capital asset (sales proceeds − adjusted basis); however, a gain or loss is not generally recognized until the short sale is closed. The holding period used to classify the sale as short-term or long-term is determined in the usual manner using the purchase (cover) as the acquisition date and the delivery as the disposition date.

The individual recognizes a $200 gain [(100 shares × $10 per share sold) − (100 shares × $8 per share purchased)]. Because the purchase (cover) and disposition (delivery) occurred on the same day (the stock was not held longer than a year), the gain is short-term
questions.explanationJa: 空売りは借りた株式を高値で売り、後に安値で買い戻して返却することで利益を狙う取引である。損益は通常の資本資産と同様に計算し、原則として空売りを決済した時点で認識する。利益は100株 × $10 − 100株 × $8 = $200となる。保有期間は買戻し日から引渡し日までで判定し、同じ日に行われているため1年以内であり、$200の短期キャピタルゲインとなる。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Property Tax Transactions Q.40

questions.stem: A married individual invested in Section 1244 small business stock in Year 1. In Year 7, the individual sold the stock at a loss of $157,000. There were no other stock transactions during Year 7. If the taxpayer files a joint return, how much loss can the taxpayer deduct in Year 7?
questions.explanation:
Individual taxpayers may deduct up to $3,000 of a net capital loss each year. Any unused loss is carried forward indefinitely.

However, to incentivize investment in small business, a loss on Section 1244 stock allows individuals to reclassify part of a capital loss to an ordinary loss, thus avoiding the $3,000 limitation. The statutory amount reclassified as an ordinary loss is $50,000 ($100,000 if married filing jointly). Any excess remains a capital loss. To qualify for Section 1244 treatment, an individual must be the stock's original purchaser.

In this scenario, because the individual is married and filing a joint return, a $100,000 ordinary loss (Section 1244 loss) is deductible. The remaining $57,000 capital loss ($157,000 − $100,000) is limited to a current-year deduction of $3,000 with the balance carried forward indefinitely. The taxpayer may deduct $103,000 ($100,000 + $3,000).
questions.explanationJa: 個人のキャピタルロスの控除は年$3,000までだが、Section 1244株式の損失は夫婦合算申告なら$100,000まで通常損失として控除できる。$157,000の損失のうち$100,000が通常損失となり、残り$57,000はキャピタルロスとして当年は$3,000のみ控除でき、残額は無期限に繰り越す。したがって当年度の控除額は$100,000 + $3,000 = $103,000である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Property Tax Transactions Q.41

questions.stem: Aviary Corp. sold a building for $600,000. Aviary received a down payment of $120,000 as well as annual principal payments of $120,000 for each of the subsequent 4 years. Aviary purchased the building for $500,000 and claimed depreciation of $80,000. What amount of gain should Aviary report in the year of sale using the installment method?
questions.explanation: Aviary Corp.'s adjusted basis is $420,000 ($500,000 cost − $80,000 depreciation). In addition, Aviary has a gross profit of $180,000 ($600,000 sales price − $420,000 adjusted basis). Therefore, the gross profit percent is 30% ($180,000 gross profit ÷ $600,000 contract amount) of the payment received. Accordingly, $36,000 (30% × $120,000 down payment) of the payment received in the year of sale should be reported.
questions.explanationJa: 建物の調整後基礎価額は$500,000 − $80,000 = $420,000で、売上総利益は$600,000 − $420,000 = $180,000である。売上総利益率は$180,000 ÷ $600,000 = 30%となる。割賦販売法では受け取った元本にこの率を掛けて利益を認識するため、売却年度の頭金$120,000に対する利益は30% × $120,000 = $36,000である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Property Tax Transactions Q.42

questions.stem: A sole proprietor of a farm implement store sold a truck for $15,000 that had been used to make service calls. The truck cost $30,000 three years ago, and $21,360 depreciation was taken. What is the appropriate classification of the $6,360 gain for tax purposes?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Section 1231 (Property Used in the Trade or Business and Involuntary Conversions) gain.

questions.explanation: In this scenario, the taxpayer recognized a $6,360 gain. The lesser of $6,360 gain or $21,360 accumulated depreciation is recaptured as ordinary income. Therefore, $6,360 is reported as ordinary income. Because there is no remaining gain, nothing is taxed as a Section 1231 gain
questions.explanationJa: トラックの調整後基礎価額は$30,000 − $21,360 = $8,640で、売却益は$15,000 − $8,640 = $6,360である。事業用動産（Section 1245資産）では、売却益と減価償却累計額のいずれか少ない額を通常所得としてリキャプチャーする。売却益$6,360は減価償却累計額$21,360より少ないため全額が通常所得となり、Section 1231利得として残る額はない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Property Tax Transactions Q.43

questions.stem: Bank Corp.'s voting stock is owned by the following individuals: Farber, 25%; Farber's mother, 15%; Farber's father, 40%; and Grosset, an unrelated person, 20%. Farber's sister sold equipment to Bank at a loss. For the purposes of determining whether the sister's loss is deductible under the related party rules, what percentage of Bank's stock, if any, does the sister constructively own?
questions.explanation: In this scenario, no shares are directly owned by Farber's sister. However, the shares owned by the sister's brother (Farber, 25%), mother (Farber's mother, 15%), and father (Farber's father, 40%) are considered constructively (indirectly) owned by the sister. Therefore, Farber's sister's constructive ownership is 80% (25% + 15% + 40%) and $0 loss is deductible
questions.explanationJa: 関連当事者規定の判定では、本人の家族（兄弟姉妹・両親など）が所有する株式を本人が間接的に所有しているとみなす（みなし所有）。Farberの姉妹は直接株式を所有していないが、兄弟であるFarberの25%、母の15%、父の40%をみなし所有する。したがってみなし所有割合は25% + 15% + 40% = 80%となり、Bank Corp.への売却損は控除できない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Property Tax Transactions Q.44

questions.stem: A corporation's capital losses are

choices.label: A
choices.text: Deductible only to the extent of the corporation's capital gains.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Deductible from the corporation's ordinary income to the extent of $3,000.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Carried back 3 years and forward 15 years.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Forfeited if the corporation had no capital gains in the year in which the capital losses were incurred.

questions.explanation: Corporate capital losses may be used only to offset capital gains. Unused net capital losses are carried back 3 years to offset any prior capital gains. Any remaining loss is carried forward to offset future capital gains for up to 5 years. All corporate net capital loss carrybacks and carryforwards are considered short-term capital losses regardless of their actual nature
questions.explanationJa: 法人のキャピタルロスはキャピタルゲインとのみ相殺でき、通常所得からは控除できない。未使用の純キャピタルロスは3年繰り戻して過去のキャピタルゲインと相殺し、残りは5年繰り越す。繰り戻し・繰り越されたロスは本来の性質にかかわらず短期キャピタルロスとして扱う。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Property Tax Transactions Q.45

questions.stem:
A C corporation incurred a $438,000 capital loss in Year 4 and has the following tax information:

Year 4 | Year 3 | Year 2 | Year 1
Capital gain (loss) | ($438,000) | $11,000 | $21,000 | $0
Taxable income (loss) | 750,000 | 31,000 | 17,000 | 25,000

What amount of capital loss is available for carryover to future tax years?
questions.explanation:
In this scenario, the corporation had a net capital loss in Year 4 of $438,000, for which no deduction is allowed. The loss is carried back three years, starting with Year 1, to offset prior year capital gains. However, in Year 2, if all the $21,000 capital gains were offset, an NOL would occur because Year 2 taxable income is only $17,000. Accordingly, the carryback for Year 2 is limited to taxable income. After the carrybacks, the corporation will have a $410,000 capital loss remaining (as shown below) to be carried forward for five years.

Year 4 capital loss | ($438,000)
Less Year 1 capital gains (none) | 0
Less Year 2 taxable income offset* | 17,000
Less Year 3 capital gains offset | 11,000
Capital loss carryforward balance | ($410,000)
*Limited to taxable income:
questions.explanationJa: Year 4の純キャピタルロス$438,000は当期に控除できず、3年前のYear 1から順に繰り戻す。Year 1はキャピタルゲインがないため相殺額はない。Year 2のキャピタルゲインは$21,000だが、全額相殺すると課税所得$17,000を超えて純損失（NOL）が生じるため、繰り戻しは課税所得の$17,000に制限される。Year 3はキャピタルゲイン$11,000と相殺する。繰越額は$438,000 − $17,000 − $11,000 = $410,000となり、5年間繰り越す。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Property Tax Transactions Q.46

questions.stem: An LLC exchanged an office building with a fair market value of $550,000 and an adjusted basis of $220,000 for a shopping center with a fair market value of $600,000. If the LLC paid an additional $50,000 to complete the exchange, what amount of gain, if any, would the LLC realize?
questions.explanation: The realized gain is the amount realized minus the adjusted basis given up. The LLC received a shopping center worth $600,000 and gave up the office building (adjusted basis $220,000) plus $50,000 of cash, so the realized gain is $600,000 - ($220,000 + $50,000) = $330,000. Equivalently, the gain is the building's fair market value of $550,000 less its adjusted basis of $220,000 = $330,000. The $50,000 of cash paid by the LLC is not boot received, so it does not create gain.
questions.explanationJa: 実現利益は、受け取った財産の公正価値から、引き渡した資産の調整後基礎価額と支払ったボートを差し引いて求める。LLCは公正価値$600,000のショッピングセンターを受け取り、簿価$220,000の事務所ビルと現金$50,000を引き渡した。したがって実現利益は$600,000 − ($220,000 + $50,000) = $330,000である。事務所ビルの公正価値$550,000から簿価$220,000を引いても同額になる。支払った現金$50,000は受取ボートではないため、利益を生じさせない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Property Tax Transactions Q.47

questions.stem: A cash-basis taxpayer made a bona fide, nonbusiness loan to an acquaintance in year 1. At the end of year 2, it is determined that the taxpayer will likely be able to collect only 20% of the principal, and no interest has been or will be collected. How should the loss be treated for tax purposes in year 2?

choices.label: A
choices.text: 80% of the principal, up to $3,000, is deductible in year 2.

choices.label: B
choices.text: None of the loss is deductible in year 2.

choices.label: C
choices.text: 80% of the principal and 80% of the interest are deductible in year 2.

choices.label: D
choices.text: 80% of the principal, but none of the interest, is deductible in year 2.

questions.explanation:
Bona fide debt is an obligation established with (1) an expectation of a determinable amount of repayment, and (2) an intent to enforce the obligation. Should a bona fide debt become partially worthless, loss recognition is determined by whether the debt was created/acquired in connection with the taxpayer's trade or business.

Partial losses related to bona fide business debt are recognized the year incurred; however, partial losses related to bona fide nonbusiness debt are not allowed. Bona fide nonbusiness debt is treated as a loss only the year it becomes wholly worthless (0% of principal is collectible).

Because the taxpayer's bona fide debt is partially worthless (20% collectible/80% uncollectible) and is nonbusiness debt, this loss is not allowed in Year 2 (or in any year until wholly worthless).
questions.explanationJa: 貸付金が真正な債権である場合、部分的に回収不能となったときの損失の扱いは事業上の債権かどうかで異なる。事業上の債権は部分的な貸倒れでもその年に損失を認識できるが、非事業上の債権は完全に回収不能（回収可能額0%）となった年にしか損失として扱えない。本問の債権は非事業上のものであり、元本の20%は回収できる見込みのため、Year 2には損失を一切控除できない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Property Tax Transactions Q.48

questions.stem: An individual taxpayer purchased a scooter costing $1,000 and a jet ski costing $8,000 both for personal use. During the current year, the taxpayer sold the scooter for $800 and the jet ski for $9,000. What gain or loss does the taxpayer recognize?
questions.explanation:
There are three types of losses incurred by individual taxpayers that are deductible (recognized) for tax purposes. These include losses resulting from:

A trade of business

Transactions entered into for profit (investments)

Casualty and theft losses (if in a federally declared disaster area)

In general, no loss is allowed from the sale of personal use assets (scooter, jet ski, automobile). These losses are considered consumption losses (based on usage rather than a decline in value). However, due to the all-inclusive approach to gross income (income from whatever source derived), gains from the sale of personal use assets are recognized (taxable). Unlike capital gains and losses, netting of personal gains and losses is not permitted.

In this scenario, the taxpayer has a $200 loss ($800 sales price − $1,000 cost) and a $1,000 gain ($9,000 sales price − $8,000 cost) from personal use assets. Because the loss is not one of the three types permitted, the loss is not recognized. However, the $1,000 gain is recognized
questions.explanationJa: 個人が損失を控除できるのは、事業から生じた損失、営利目的の取引（投資）による損失、および災害・盗難損失に限られる。私用資産の売却損は消費による価値減少とみなされ控除できない。一方、あらゆる源泉からの所得が総所得に含まれるため、私用資産の売却益は課税される。私用資産間で損益を相殺することもできない。したがってスクーターの損失$200（$800 − $1,000）は認識されず、ジェットスキーの利益$1,000（$9,000 − $8,000）は認識される。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Property Tax Transactions Q.49

questions.stem: An individual purchased two automobiles for personal use. Automobile 1 had an adjusted basis of $20,000, and Automobile 2 had an adjusted basis of $10,000. The individual sold Automobile 1 for $15,000 and Automobile 2 for $15,000. What gain or loss should the individual recognize on the sales of the automobiles?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Automobile 1, loss of $5,000; Automobile 2, gain of $5,000.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Automobile 1, loss of $0; Automobile 2, gain of $5,000.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Automobile 1, loss of $5,000; Automobile 2, gain of $0.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Automobile 1, loss of $0; Automobile 2, gain of $0.

questions.explanation:
Personal use property refers to property owned for personal, living, and/or family use (not used for business or investment). Unless exempted by law, individual taxpayers must recognize gains on the sale of personal use property. Conversely, individual taxpayers can not recognize (deduct) losses on the sale of personal use property because any loss in value is considered personal consumption.

The individual realizes a loss of $5,000 ($15,000 sale price − $20,000 adjusted basis) on Automobile 1 but realizes a gain of $5,000 ($15,000 sale price − $10,000 adjusted basis) on Automobile 2. No loss is recognized on Automobile 1
questions.explanationJa: 私用資産は、法律で非課税とされない限り売却益は認識しなければならないが、売却損は個人的な消費とみなされ控除できない。自動車1は$15,000 − $20,000 = $5,000の損失が実現するが、私用資産のため認識される損失は$0である。自動車2は$15,000 − $10,000 = $5,000の利益が実現し、そのまま認識される。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Property Tax Transactions Q.50

questions.stem: An individual taxpayer sells stock with a basis of $11,000 to her brother for $7,600. The value of the stock 30 days prior to the sale is $9,600. The taxpayer has no other capital asset transactions during the year. What amount, if any, can the taxpayer deduct on her tax return for the loss sustained?
questions.explanation: In this scenario, the taxpayer has a realized loss of $3,400 ($7,600 sale price − $11,000 basis). However, this loss is disallowed ($0 deduction) because the transaction was between siblings (related parties).
questions.explanationJa: 納税者の実現損失は売却価額$7,600から基礎価額$11,000を引いた$3,400である。しかし兄弟姉妹は関連当事者に当たるため、この損失は否認され、控除額は$0となる。売却30日前の株価は損失の計算に関係しない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Property Tax Transactions Q.51

questions.stem: Spark Inc., a C corporation, owned an office building for several years. The building was originally purchased for $100,000 and has accumulated depreciation of $28,000 using straight-line depreciation under the modified accelerated cost recovery system. If Spark sold the building for $110,000, what amount is recaptured as ordinary gain from this transaction?
questions.explanation:
Specifically, Section 291 requires C corporations to recapture a statutory 20% of the lesser of accumulated depreciation or the total gain as ordinary income. Any remaining gain is Section 1231 gain, which is generally treated as a capital gain.

In this scenario, the building has an adjusted basis of $72,000 ($100,000 cost − $28,000 accumulated depreciation) resulting in a gain of $38,000 ($110,000 sale price − $72,000 adjusted basis) when sold. Since the $28,000 depreciation taken is less than the gain, Spark Inc. should use depreciation to calculate recapture (20% × $28,000 depreciation). Therefore, Spark must recapture and report $5,600 as ordinary gain.
questions.explanationJa: C法人がSection 1250資産（建物）を売却益で処分すると、Section 291により、減価償却累計額と売却益のいずれか少ない額の20%を通常所得としてリキャプチャーする。調整後基礎価額は$100,000 − $28,000 = $72,000、売却益は$110,000 − $72,000 = $38,000である。減価償却累計額$28,000の方が少ないためこれを用い、リキャプチャー額は$28,000 × 20% = $5,600となる。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Property Tax Transactions Q.52

questions.stem: A taxpayer gave a gift of land worth $90,000 to a cousin. The land's original cost to the taxpayer was $30,000. As a result of the transfer, the taxpayer paid a gift tax of $12,000. Assuming an annual gift exclusion of $15,000, what is the cousin's basis in the land?
questions.explanation:
Gifted property has appreciated in value when its FMV at the time of transfer is greater than the donor's　adjusted basis. Generally, for appreciated property, the donee's basis and holding period are the same as the donor's. Therefore, when the donee sells the property, any gain (or loss) is based on the carried-over basis.

However, if the donor pays　gift tax, the portion of the tax paid attributable to the property's appreciation at the date of the gift is added to the donee's basis. The formula used to determine this amount is:

(Appreciation / Net taxable gift) × Gift tax paid

The net taxable gift = FMV minus annual gift tax exclusion.

In this scenario, because the gift was appreciated property ($90,000 FMV when gifted > $30,000 adjusted basis), the cousin assumed the carryover basis ($30,000) plus a portion of the gift tax paid by the taxpayer. The portion of the gift tax is calculated as:

($90,000 FMV-$30,000 basis)➗($90,000 FMV-$15,000 gift tax exclusion)×$12,000 gift tax=$9,600

Therefore, the cousin's basis in the land is $39,600 ($30,000 + $9,600).
questions.explanationJa: 値上がりした資産の贈与では、受贈者は贈与者の基礎価額$30,000を引き継ぐ。ただし贈与者が贈与税を支払った場合は、税額のうち値上がり益に対応する部分を基礎価額に加算する。加算額は（値上がり益 ÷ 課税対象贈与額）× 贈与税で、課税対象贈与額は公正価値から年間非課税枠を引いた額である。($90,000 − $30,000) ÷ ($90,000 − $15,000) × $12,000 = $9,600となり、基礎価額は$30,000 + $9,600 = $39,600である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Property Tax Transactions Q.53

questions.stem: A taxpayer gave a gift of stock worth $10,000 to a nephew. The taxpayer's basis in the stock was $15,000. The nephew sold the stock to an unrelated party for $11,000. What amount of gain or loss should the nephew report as a result of this sale?
questions.explanation: In this scenario, when the property was gifted, the FMV was less than the donor's adjusted basis. Therefore, the nephew had dual basis for the property ($15,000 if sold later for a gain and $10,000 if sold for a loss). However, because the sales price of $11,000 fell between the two bases ($10,000 < $11,000 < $15,000), no gain or loss was recognized; the nephew should report $0 as a result of the sale.
questions.explanationJa: 贈与時の公正価値$10,000が贈与者の基礎価額$15,000を下回るため、甥は二重の基礎価額を持つ（利益の計算には$15,000、損失の計算には$10,000）。売却額$11,000は両者の間にあるため、利益の計算では$11,000 − $15,000で損失、損失の計算では$11,000 − $10,000で利益となり、どちらも成立しない。したがって損益は認識されず、報告額は$0である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Property Tax Transactions Q.54

questions.stem: Which of the following improvements would be considered an adaptation to the property?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Costs incurred to fix defective machinery that existed prior to acquisition.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Costs incurred to alter equipment to be used in an entity's manufacturing operation that was previously used for research and development.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Cost incurred to reconstruct a warehouse's support beams to comply with new building codes.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Costs incurred to convert existing manufacturing equipment to robotic manufacturing equipment.

questions.explanation:
Tax regulations specify the treatment of costs incurred for acquiring, maintaining, improving, repairing, and replacing tangible real and personal property. Costs for repairs and maintenance are expensed as incurred.

However, amounts paid to improve tangible property are required to be capitalized if the costs incurred result in a betterment, an adaptation, or restoration to the property. These costs are capitalized because the asset's useful life is usually extended.
